solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Foreign article with early warning about split

indicators.note: about says the warning word goes round the article, holding it inside

parts.note: cave! (Latin 'beware') is old schoolboy slang shouted as a warning that a teacher is coming
le is the French word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A news story about a foreign piece of writing that warned early of a division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the schoolboy lookout's cry round the article; 'early warning' is not a radar system here.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave something is to split it apart, as with a cleaver.

clue.text: Serve Indian dish elevated by lime peel

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word up the column reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: dal is a lentil dish from Indian cooking

indicators.note: the peel is the outside of a fruit, so only the outer letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to serve a curry topped with a little lime zest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns DAL upwards to LAD; 'peel' gives the outer letters of lime, L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To ladle food is to serve it out with a big spoon.

clue.text: Discrimination in hit parade after a fashion

indicators.note: after a fashion means done in some loose way, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A complaint that the music charts are unfair to some artists.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was South Africa's system of racial segregation, an extreme form of discrimination.

clue.text: Unfamiliar regime for foreigner

indicators.note: unfamiliar suggests the word regime is made strange, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An outsider finds the government system strange.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigre is someone who has left their own country to live abroad, so a foreigner there.

clue.text: Suggest jazz fan checks maverick record company

indicators.note: checks in the sense of holds or restrains, so the label holds the jazz fan inside it

parts.note: an indie is an independent label, a maverick outside the big companies
cat is old jazz slang for a fan or player

explanation.surface: A jazz lover keeps an eye on an unorthodox record label, hinting at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checks' is the container signal, in its sense of holding back, not inspecting.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to point to or hint at something, a synonym of suggest.

clue.text: Popular article on Mrs Cameron, one's ultimate inspiration all together

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the is the definite article
Samantha (Sam) Cameron is the wife of former UK prime minister David Cameron

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so the final letter of the word one is taken

parts.note: inspiration in its literal sense is breathing in, a breath

explanation.surface: A gossip item about a prime minister's wife being someone's chief inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Said in the same breath means said at the same moment, all at once.

clue.text: Peter out wanting run before date getting late

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to peter out is to dwindle or decrease
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone named Peter leaves before a running date, ending up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' drops the run; 'before' sets the order. 'Peter' looks like a name but is part of the verb peter out.
explanation.definitionFit: Late in the sense of recently dead, as in 'the late king', means deceased.

clue.text: Maniac Ricky making comeback will box roughly

indicators.note: making comeback says the enclosed letters are read backwards
will box means the two words will enclose the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A crazed boxer called Ricky returning to the ring for a rough bout.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'will box roughly' as the definition, but 'will box' is the indicator that Maniac Ricky holds the letters; 'roughly' alone defines. Reading ACRIC backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa, from Latin, is used before dates to mean approximately.

clue.text: Perk up Spooner's fish pie

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

parts.note: hake is a sea fish
a tart is a pie

explanation.surface: Cheer up, the clergyman says, over a fishy pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of HAKE TART gives TAKE HART, which sounds like the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heart is to regain courage or cheer up.

clue.text: Impractical fancy heel before one that's conservative

parts.note: a fancy is a notion or idea
a ship heels or lists when it leans over
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fancy footwear judged unworkable next to the sensible pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' and 'heel' look like shoes but are a noun for a notion and a verb for leaning; 'before' just sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealistic plan aims at perfection, often at the expense of practicality.

clue.text: Comb for one who's gone thin?

definitions.meaning: to search through carefully, as with a garden tool's tines
a very thin person, from the phrase thin as a ...

explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a toothed tool used to comb soil, and thin as a rake describes a skinny person.

clue.text: In the house on the house?

definitions.text: In the house on the house?

parts.words: In the house on the house?
parts.note: living in a home where the lodging is free, as drinks 'on the house' cost nothing

explanation.definitionFit: Living without paying any charge for one's accommodation is the meaning described.

clue.text: A year taken over course of action could suggest inertia

indicators.note: taken over means placed round, so A and the year sit either side of the course

parts.note: a path is a course or way of acting

explanation.surface: A year spent on one plan may point to sluggishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is a lack of interest or energy, a mental inertia.

clue.text: Man, say, in Paisley predominantly

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the town's name, making up most of it

explanation.surface: A man found in the Scottish town of Paisley, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'predominantly' notes that the answer takes up most of PAISLEY. 'Man' is the Isle of Man, so 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea, an example of an island.

clue.text: Three-chord wonders with same old same old?

definitions.meaning: a British rock band famous for simple three-chord songs
the existing state of affairs, unchanged

explanation.definitionFit: Status Quo is a British boogie-rock band, and status quo is Latin for things as they stand.

clue.text: Ace crew welcoming Clapton in US

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the guitarist goes inside

parts.note: to crew a ship is to man it
Eric Clapton is the English rock guitarist

explanation.surface: A top crew in America takes the guitarist on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crew' looks like a noun but is the verb man.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything or anyone belonging to the United States is called American.

clue.text: It's ironic somehow about North wasting nothing essential

indicators.note: about means round, so the mix goes around the compass letter
somehow says the letters of the phrase are put together in some other way
wasting means losing, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of the two words
O is the zero shape standing for nothing

explanation.surface: Somebody remarks that it is odd that the North wastes what is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: ITSIRONIC loses its O, takes in N, and the resulting letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intrinsic belongs to a thing's basic nature, so it is essential to it.

clue.text: Key international alliance semi-liable for Asia Minor

parts.note: A is a musical key
NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization

indicators.note: semi means half, so the first half of the word liable is taken

explanation.surface: A crucial global alliance considered partly responsible for events in Asia Minor.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia is the large peninsula forming most of Turkey, historically called Asia Minor.

clue.text: Level with Mafia boss, and yours truly may be sorry

parts.note: par means equal or level, as in on a par
a don is a Mafia chief
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: Squaring up with the Godfather, the speaker may come to regret it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pardon me is a polite apology, said just like sorry.

clue.text: Thank you, thank you, and farewell

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
ta again, British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A thank-you twice over, then goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is a British informal way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Open fancy drapes

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine, so the letters are reimagined in a new order

explanation.surface: Pull back the elaborate curtains.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread something is to open it out, as with wings or a map.

clue.text: Something said somewhere bringing one in for a top-level meeting

indicators.note: bringing means introducing a new letter
in for means in place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: summat is how something is said in northern English dialect
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A remark made at some venue brings a person into a high-level conference.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMMAT is dialect 'something'; I replaces its A, the 'a' in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is a meeting between heads of government, the highest level of talks.

clue.text: Setter a gutless toady? That's rich

parts.note: a setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: gutless means with the insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: The compiler calls a cowardly flatterer rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' looks like cowardly but means emptied: TOADY loses its middle to leave TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaty describes something rich and substantial, like a meaty novel.

clue.text: Constantly importing ripe bananas, all returned as spare

indicators.note: all returned says the whole assembly is read backwards
importing means taking in, so the mix goes inside the word for always

parts.note: ever means always or constantly

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the word ripe is mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone keeps bringing in ripe fruit, all sent back as extras.
explanation.walkthrough: EVER holds EIRP (from ripe), giving EVEIRPER, which reads backwards to the answer. 'spare' looks like an adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprieve someone is to spare them from punishment.

clue.text: French behold endless electronic material

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: voila is French for 'see there' or behold

explanation.surface: A Frenchman points out an electronic gadget without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Voile is a light, semi-transparent cotton fabric used for curtains.

clue.text: Element in a Q&A about university

indicators.note: about means round, so the question and answer go round the university

parts.note: Q and A stand for question and answer

explanation.surface: A chemistry element comes up in a question session about college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' means one of the classical four, water, not a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is Latin for water, one of the four classical elements.

clue.text: Management requires author's following to change sides initially

indicators.note: changing sides swaps right for left, and initially says it is the first letter

parts.note: an author's readership is the body of people who read their books

explanation.surface: Bosses need a writer's fan base to switch allegiance at first.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for right and L for left, so the first letter swaps from R to L.
explanation.definitionFit: Leadership means the people directing an organisation, its management.

clue.text: Fry (or similar) batter amply hot

indicators.note: to batter is to beat, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: Frying, or something like it, coats batter well when hot.
explanation.walkthrough: Fry is Stephen Fry, the famously wide-knowledged British broadcaster, not cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymath is a person of wide learning, as Stephen Fry is often called.

clue.text: Fiat's ad-men carpeted regularly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A car maker's advertising staff get a dressing-down at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiat' looks like the car brand but is the Latin-derived word for an order.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative order, a decree.
